summary: Rural digital-inclusion project for seniors with mixed structure (registered small-group courses, open monthly drop-in, volunteer helpers); no application, persona must be interviewed.

traps.what: Existing data: course registration list (23 entries with age and village) and a drop-in 'question book' with topic per question, no names (approx. 140 entries since Feb 2026).
traps.pass: Measurement frame lists both the course registration list and the drop-in question book (topic log) as existing data.
traps.partial: Only one of the two named.

traps.what: The cooperative bank's foundation funds the project after the bank closed its local branch in June 2025; it explicitly hopes more seniors will use online banking; continuation decision after a board presentation in May 2027. The district only wants participant/event counts.
traps.pass: Stakeholders include the bank foundation with its specific expectation (online-banking uptake, linked to the branch closure), and the measurement frame names the May 2027 presentation as a key use.
traps.partial: Bank foundation listed as funder/stakeholder without its specific expectation, or the May 2027 presentation missing.

traps.what: Persona proposes 'all seniors in the municipality (over 2,600 people)' as target group.
traps.pass: Focus groups are narrower than all seniors of the municipality and reflect the mixed structure (e.g., course participants as a fixed group vs. drop-in visitors; volunteers as separate/indirect group).
traps.partial: Target group narrowed, but course participants and drop-in visitors are not distinguished, or all 65+ remain a focus group.

traps.what: 19 of 23 course participants are from the main village; nobody yet from two outlying villages (almost no buses); the drop-in no longer rotates through villages; isolated seniors without a smartphone are practically not reached (church senior cafés in two villages do reach them).
traps.pass: Target groups, problem tree or impact logic explicitly reflect the reach gap (outlying villages/mobility, isolated seniors not reached), e.g., as a limitation, external factor or critical assumption; the project profile does not claim the drop-in runs in every village.
traps.partial: Reach gap mentioned only in open points, or only one aspect (mobility or isolated seniors) reflected.

traps.what: Real drivers: most participants want WhatsApp/video contact with children and grandchildren; second driver is the bank branch closure forcing app-based banking. Telemedicine was the persona's own idea, nobody asked for it.
traps.pass: Problem tree / causes for seniors include both the wish for family contact (distant family) and the closure of local services/bank branch (everyday services moving online); telemedicine is not presented as a demonstrated need.
traps.partial: Only one of the two drivers appears, or telemedicine is kept as a main need.

traps.what: Persona proposes (a) 'seniors live independently at home longer and are no longer lonely' and (b) 'we offer 4 courses a year and a drop-in in every village' as goals.
traps.pass: No goal attributes longer independent living or the elimination of loneliness to the project, and no goal is an activity/output. Goals sit mainly on levels 4-5 (e.g., confidently making video calls, using the banking app, recognising scam messages); any level-6 goal is modest and time-bound; the broad aim appears at most in the level-7 contribution sentence.
traps.partial: One of the two pushes remains, or the level-6 goal is softened but still claims reduced loneliness/independent living for all participants.

traps.what: In March 2026 two participants received 'Hallo Mama' scam messages; one lost 1,800 EUR, and she and two friends went back to using the phone only for calls.
traps.pass: Unintended effects include exposure to online fraud/scams (and/or withdrawal after a bad experience), AND scam awareness appears as an activity, goal or indicator.
traps.partial: Fraud named as a generic risk without an activity/goal response, or scam awareness added without listing the unintended effect.

traps.what: Persona asserts 'video calls with grandchildren reduce loneliness', evidence 'Erfahrung halt' (one anecdote).
traps.pass: This link/assumption is listed with an honest evidence basis (own experience/anecdote or unsure, not research or own data) and marked critical, or turned into a learning question.
traps.partial: Assumption listed but evidence rated as solid or not marked critical.

traps.what: Only 4 of 10 trained volunteers are still active; participants call them privately in the evenings; one quit ('I'm not a hotline').
traps.pass: Impact logic reflects volunteer capacity: e.g., unintended effect of volunteer overload/private calls, and/or a critical assumption or input noting only 4 of 10 active volunteers.
traps.partial: Volunteers listed only as a generic input without the capacity problem.

traps.what: Many participants are hard of hearing and have poor eyesight; a two-page small-print feedback form after course 1 was mostly left blank; phone follow-ups do not work; face-to-face talk in the course works well.
traps.pass: Data collection methods for seniors are adapted: face-to-face/oral in course sessions (e.g., short guided round, large-print one-page sheet, assisted completion); no phone survey and no long small-print questionnaire as main method; consent handled in a simple, accessible way.
traps.partial: Methods partly adapted (e.g., in-person but still a long written questionnaire), or phone survey still planned.
